title: Module Assessment: Generators & Iterators (PY_223 to PY_229)

slides.title: Module 4 Overview
slides.prompt: Assessment covering Iterators, Generators, yield, yield from, send(), and itertools.

slides.title: Question 1: Iterator Protocol
slides.prompt: Which two methods constitute Python Iterator Protocol?

slides.title: Question 2: Generator Keyword
slides.prompt: Fill in keyword that pauses function execution and returns a value to caller.

slides.title: Question 3: Stop Iteration
slides.prompt: Which exception signal end of iteration when `next()` is called?

slides.title: Question 4: Sub-generator Delegation
slides.prompt: Which syntax delegates generator iteration directly to a sub-generator or iterable?

slides.title: Question 5: Generator Expression Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in correct brackets to build a generator expression.

slides.title: Question 6: Sending Values
slides.prompt: Which method sends values into a running generator pause state?

slides.title: Question 7: Infinite Cycle
slides.prompt: Fill in function from `itertools` that cycles infinitely over iterable.

slides.title: Question 8: Generator Memory Usage
slides.prompt: Why are generators memory efficient compared to lists?
options: Lazy evaluation (calculates items on the fly)
slides.correctAnswer: Lazy evaluation (calculates items on the fly)

slides.title: Question 9: Itertools Chain
options: Combines multiple iterables sequentially into single iterator
slides.correctAnswer: Combines multiple iterables sequentially into single iterator

slides.title: Question 10: Closing Generator
slides.prompt: Fill in method called to stop generator and raise `GeneratorExit` inside it.

slides.title: Question 11: Built-in Iter Function
slides.prompt: What is the second argument of 2-argument sentinel form of `iter(func, sentinel)`?
options: Value that triggers StopIteration when func() returns it
slides.correctAnswer: Value that triggers StopIteration when func() returns it

slides.title: Question 12: Itertools Islice
slides.prompt: How does `itertools.islice()` differ from standard list slicing `lst[start:stop]`?
options: Works lazily on iterators without creating list in memory
slides.correctAnswer: Works lazily on iterators without creating list in memory

slides.title: Question 13: Throw Exception
slides.prompt: Fill in method used to raise an exception inside generator.
